title: Well-foundedness of the next_slot order by strengthening to finite-and-acyclic
intent: Replace the goal `wf {(next, p). next_slot p (cdt_list s) (cdt s) = Some next}` in one step by the stronger conjunction `finite ... ∧ acyclic ...` through the library rule `finite_acyclic_wf`, so well-foundedness of the next-slot traversal is assembled from two independent halves: a finiteness bound (via `cte_at_next_slot`, `cte_at_next_slot'` and `finite_depth`) and a no-loop fact (`next_slot_no_loop`).

parent.name: wf_next_slot
parent.statement:
lemma wf_next_slot:
  notes split_paired_All[simp del] split_paired_Ex[simp del]
  shows
  "\<lbrakk>valid_mdb s; valid_list s\<rbrakk>
    \<Longrightarrow> wf {(next, p). next_slot p (cdt_list s) (cdt s) = Some next}"

children.name: next_slot_no_loop
children.statement:
lemma next_slot_no_loop:
  notes split_paired_All[simp del] split_paired_Ex[simp del]
  shows "\<lbrakk>valid_list_2 t m; no_mloop m; finite_depth m\<rbrakk>
    \<Longrightarrow> x \<notin> next_slot_set x t m"
children.closed_by: apply(rule notI) then case_tac "m x"; the None branch closes via next_slot_setD + next_sib_set_not_self, the Some branch via next_slot_set_after_in_list + next_sib_set_not_self; done

children.name: cte_at_next_slot
children.statement:
lemma cte_at_next_slot:
  notes split_paired_All[simp del] split_paired_Ex[simp del]
  shows "\<lbrakk>valid_list s; valid_mdb s; finite_depth (cdt s)\<rbrakk>
    \<Longrightarrow> next_slot p (cdt_list s) (cdt s) = Some n \<Longrightarrow> cte_at p s"
children.closed_by: split next_slot_def on if_split_asm; the child/next branches close via next_childD / next_sibD plus descendants_of_cte_at2 / descendants_of_cte_at and next_not_child_termination; done

children.name: cte_at_next_slot'
children.statement:
lemma cte_at_next_slot':
  "\<lbrakk>valid_list s; valid_mdb s; finite_depth (cdt s)\<rbrakk>
    \<Longrightarrow> next_slot p (cdt_list s) (cdt s) = Some n \<Longrightarrow> cte_at n s"
children.closed_by: split next_slot_def, then an induction with next_not_child_pinduct2; each case closes via descendants_of_cte_at2 / descendants_of_cte_at and next_sibD; done

children.name: finite_depth
children.statement:
lemma finite_depth:
  notes split_paired_All[simp del] split_paired_Ex[simp del]
  shows "valid_mdb s \<Longrightarrow> finite_depth (cdt s)"
children.closed_by: finite_subset + cte_wp_at_set_finite for finiteness, then a strict-subset cardinality argument closed by psubset_card_mono; done

applicability.goal_shape: A `wf R` goal where `R` is a binary relation over a finite state graph — here the next_slot traversal `{(next, p). next_slot p (cdt_list s) (cdt s) = Some next}` of the capability-derivation tree — and where finiteness and acyclicity of `R` are each easier to prove than a direct well-foundedness argument.
applicability.use_when: the relation's pairs can be bounded by a known finite carrier (`cte_wp_at_set_finite`), acyclicity reduces to a no-loop lemma `x ∉ R⁺ x`, and the two halves of `finite_acyclic_wf` each have their own named lemma.
applicability.avoid_when: `R` is infinite or well-founded only via a measure/witness rather than by finiteness (e.g. the natural-number `<` order); acyclicity needs more than a plain no-loop lemma; or the two halves share so much work that a single direct proof is shorter.

consequences: Replaces one `wf R` obligation with two: `finite R` and `acyclic R`. The finiteness half must bound every pair `(next, p)` of the relation in a finite carrier — `cte_at_next_slot` / `cte_at_next_slot'` show each endpoint is a `cte_at`, so `R` is a subset of `{p. cte_wp_at ⊤ p s} × {p. cte_wp_at ⊤ p s}`, finite by `cte_wp_at_set_finite`. The acyclicity half needs a no-loop lemma whose `finite_depth (cdt s)` precondition is discharged by `finite_depth` itself. Failure modes: `finite_depth` is the real content (a 52-line cardinality argument) and its cost is inherited by both halves; `finite_acyclic_wf` yields `wf` only for literally finite relations, so the move does not reach infinite well-founded orders.
